The following is a list and timeline of [[innovation]]s as well as [[invention]]s and [[discovery (observation)|discoveries]] that involved [[British people]] or the [[United Kingdom]] including the [[history of the formation of the United Kingdom|predecessor states before the Treaty of Union in 1707]], the [[Kingdom of England]] and the [[Kingdom of Scotland]]. This list covers, but is not limited to, innovation and invention in the mechanical, electronic, and industrial fields, as well as medicine, military devices and theory, artistic and scientific discovery and innovation, and ideas in religion and ethics.

Factors that historians note spurred innovation and discovery include the 17th century [[Scientific Revolution]] and the 18th/19th century [[Industrial Revolution]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Jacob|first1=Margaret C.|title=Scientific culture and the making of the industrial west|date=1997|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=New York|isbn=978-0195082203|pages=9–11|id= {{ASIN|0195082192|country=uk}}}}</ref><ref>[[#Walker1993|Walker 1993]], pp. 187-8.</ref> Another possible influence is the British [[patent]] system which had medieval origins and was codified with the [[Patent Law Amendment Act 1852]] ([[15 & 16 Vict.]] c. 83).<ref>{{cite journal |last=Leaffer |first=Marshall A. |title=Book Review. Inventing the Industrial Revolution: The English Patent System, 1660–1800 |journal=Articles by Maurer Faculty |date=1990 |issue=666 |url=http://www.repository.law.indiana.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1663&context=facpub |postscript=none }}; {{cite book |last=MacLeod |first=Christine |title=Inventing the industrial revolution : The English patent system, 1660–1800 |date=1988 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |isbn=9780521893992 |url=http://www.cambridge.org/gb/academic/subjects/history/british-history-after-1450/inventing-industrial-revolution-english-patent-system-16601800 }}</ref>

==Prehistory==
* A 2025 study reported evidence of deliberate fire-making in [[Suffolk]], England, dating to about 400,000 years [[Before Present]]. The authors describe it as the earliest known evidence of humans making fire.<ref name="Fire">{{cite journal |last1=Davis |first1=Rob |last2=Hatch |first2=Marcus |last3=Hoare |first3=Sally |last4=Lewis |first4=Simon G. |last5=Lucas |first5=Claire |last6=Parfitt |first6=Simon A. |last7=Bello |first7=Silvia M. |last8=Lewis |first8=Mark |last9=Mansfield |first9=Jordan |last10=Najorka |first10=Jens |last11=O'Connor |first11=Simon |last12=Peglar |first12=Sylvia |last13=Sorensen |first13=Andrew |last14=Stringer |first14=Chris |last15=Ashton |first15=Nick |title=Earliest evidence of making fire |journal=Nature |date=10 December 2025 |volume=649 |issue=8097 |pages=631–637 |doi=10.1038/s41586-025-09855-6 |pmid=41372405 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09855-6#citeas |access-date=11 December 2025|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==14th century==
;1326
* [[Rectangulus]]. The rectangulus was an astronomical instrument made by Richard of Wallingford around 1326. Dissatisfied with the limitations of existing astrolabes, Richard developed the rectangulus as an instrument for spherical trigonometry and to measure the angles between planets and other astronomical bodies

== 16th century ==

[[File:Stocking Frame.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Stocking frame]]

;1589
* [[Stocking frame]]; the mechanical stocking frame knitting machine was invented by John Lee, an English inventor. Its principle of operation remains in use today.<ref>{{cite web |title=William Lee (1563-1614) |url=https://alumni.christs.cam.ac.uk/william-lee |website=Christ's College}}</ref>

== 17th century ==

[[File:Savery-engine.jpg|upright|thumb|The 1698 ''[[Thomas Savery|Savery Engine]]'']]

;1605
* [[Bacon's cipher]], a method of [[steganography]] (hiding a secret message), is devised by Sir [[Francis Bacon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ciphers of Francis Bacon|url=http://www.fbrt.org.uk/pages/essays/essay-ciphers.html|publisher=The Francis Bacon Research Trust|access-date=25 April 2015|archive-date=19 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150419122137/http://www.fbrt.org.uk/pages/essays/essay-ciphers.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;1614
* [[John Napier]] publishes his work ''[[Mirifici Logarithmorum Canonis Descriptio]]'' introducing the concept of [[logarithm]]s which simplifies mathematical calculations.<ref>Ernest William Hobson. ''John Napier and the invention of logarithms, 1614.'' The University Press, 1914.</ref><ref>''Memoirs of John Napier of Merchiston: his lineage, life, and times'' by [[Mark Napier (historian)|Mark Napier]]</ref>

;1620
* The first navigable [[submarine]] is designed by [[William Bourne (mathematician)|William Bourne]] and built by Dutchman [[Cornelius Drebbel]].

;1625
* Early experiments in water [[desalination]] are conducted by Sir [[Francis Bacon]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lenntech.com/history-water-treatment.htm |title=History of water treatment |website=Lenntech.com|access-date=22 January 2011|last=Enzler MSc|first=S.M.}}</ref>

;1657
* [[Anchor escapement]] for clock making is invented by [[Robert Hooke]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://geocities.com/CapeCanaveral/Hall/3934/anchor.html |title=The Origin and Evolution of the Anchor Clock Escapement |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091022224723/http://geocities.com/CapeCanaveral/Hall/3934/anchor.html |archive-date=October 22, 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

;1667
* A [[tin can telephone]] is devised by [[Robert Hooke]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roberthooke.org.uk/micro2.htm|title=Micrographia – Extracts From The Preface|access-date=2011-09-11|archive-date=2011-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721015647/http://www.roberthooke.org.uk/micro2.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;1668
* Sir [[Isaac Newton]] invents the first working reflecting [[telescope]].<ref name="auto2">{{cite book |last1=Murray |title=Human accomplishment : the pursuit of excellence in the arts and sciences, 800 B.C. to 1950 |publisher=HarperCollins e-books |isbn=9780061745676 |page=164 |edition=1st|date=2009-10-13 }}</ref>

;1698
* The first commercial [[steam engine|steam-powered device]], a water pump, is developed by [[Thomas Savery]].<ref name="oakes_atoz">{{cite book|title=A to Z of STS scientists|author=Elizabeth H. Oakes|publisher=Facts on File Inc|year=2002|isbn=978-0-8160-4606-5|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/tozofstsscientis0000oake}}</ref>

==18th century==
[[File:Maquina vapor Watt ETSIIM.jpg|thumb|The [[Watt steam engine]] was conceived in 1765. [[James Watt]] transformed the [[steam engine]] from a  reciprocating motion that was used for pumping to a rotating motion suited to industrial applications.  Watt and others significantly improved the efficiency of the steam engine.]]

;1701
* An improved [[seed drill]] is designed by [[Jethro Tull (agriculturist)|Jethro Tull]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Historic Figures* Jethro Tull (1674–1741)|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/history/historic_figures/tull_jethro.shtml|publisher=BBC|access-date=4 April 2015}}</ref> It is used to spread seeds around a field with a rotating handle which makes seed planting a lot easier.

;1705
* [[Edmond Halley]] makes the first prediction of a [[comet]]'s return.<ref name="auto2"/>
;1712
* The [[Newcomen atmospheric engine|first practical steam engine]] is designed by [[Thomas Newcomen]].<ref name="oakes_atoz"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/history/historic_figures/newcomen_thomas.shtml|title=Historic Figures:Thomas Newcomen (1663–1729)|publisher=BBC|access-date=6 December 2010}}</ref>
;1718
* [[Edmond Halley]] discovers [[stellar motion]].<ref name="auto2"/>

;1730
* The Rotherham [[plough]], the first plough to be widely built in factories and commercially successful, is patented by Joseph Foljambe.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Rotherham Plough|url=http://www.rotherhamweb.co.uk/h/plough.htm|website=Rotherhamweb.co.uk|access-date=5 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924092217/http://www.rotherhamweb.co.uk/h/plough.htm|archive-date=2015-09-24|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;1737
* Andrew Rodger invents the [[winnowing machine]].

;1740
* The first [[electrostatic motor]]s are developed by [[Andrew Gordon (Benedictine)|Andrew Gordon]] in the 1740s.<ref name="Gordon">{{cite book|first=Tom|last=McInally|title=The Sixth Scottish University: The Scots Colleges Abroad: 1575 to 1799|publisher=BRILL|isbn= 9789004214262|year= 2011|page=115|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yv4uBMC64tsC&q=electric+motor}}</ref>

;1744
* The earliest known reference to [[baseball]] is made in a publication, ''[[A Little Pretty Pocket-Book]]'', by [[John Newbery]]. It contains a rhymed description of "base-ball" and a [[woodcut]] that shows a field set-up somewhat similar to the modern game—though in a triangular rather than diamond configuration, and with posts instead of ground-level bases.<ref>Block (2005), pp. 139, 140, 151, 164, 178, 179, et seq.; {{cite web|author=Hellier, Cathy|url=http://www.history.org/history/teaching/enewsletter/volume2/june04/pocketbook.cfm|title=Mr. Newbery's Little Pretty Pocket-Book|access-date=2008-04-12|publisher=Colonial Williamsburg Foundation|archive-date=2011-01-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110110115349/http://www.history.org/history/teaching/enewsletter/volume2/june04/pocketbook.cfm|url-status=dead}} See [[s:A Little Pretty Pocket-book/Base-Ball|Wikisource edition of ''A Little Pretty Pocket-Book'']].</ref>

;1753
* Invention of hollow-pipe [[drainage]] is credited to Sir Hugh Dalrymple who died in 1753.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broadside eulogy dedicated to Patrick, Earl of Marchmount, Sir Hugh Dalrymple, and others|url=http://digital.nls.uk/broadsides/broadside.cfm/id/15893|publisher=National Library of Scotland|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref>
'''1761'''
* The [[marine chronometer]] is invented by [[John Harrison]]; enabling accurate nautical navigation and effectively establishing [[Greenwich]] as the ''de facto'' universal [[Prime meridian (Greenwich)|prime meridian]].
;1765
* [[James Hargreaves]] invented the [[spinning jenny]], which was a multi-[[Spindle (textiles)|spindle]] [[spinning wheel|spinning frame]], and was one of the key developments in the [[Textile manufacture during the Industrial Revolution|industrialisation]] of [[textile manufacturing]] during the early [[Industrial Revolution]].
* [[James Small (inventor)|James Small]] advances the design of the plough using mathematical methods to improve on the Scotch plough of [[James Anderson of Hermiston]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Wilson|first1=Rick|title=Scots Who Made America|date=2015|publisher=Birlinn|isbn=9780857908827|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v2KgBwAAQBAJ&q=james+anderson+scotch+plough&pg=PT127|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref>

;1767
* [[Adam Ferguson]] (1767), often known as 'The Father of Modern Sociology', publishes his work ''[[An Essay on the History of Civil Society]]''.<ref>Willcox, William Bradford; Arnstein, Walter L. (1966). The Age of Aristocracy, 1688 to 1830. Volume III of A History of England, edited by Lacey Baldwin Smith (Sixth Edition, 1992 ed.). Lexington, Massachusetts. p. 133. {{ISBN|0-669-24459-7}}.</ref>

;1776
* Scottish economist [[Adam Smith]], often known as 'The father of modern economics',<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Davis | first1 = William L | last2 = Figgins | first2 = Bob | last3 = Hedengren | first3 = David | last4 = Klein | first4 = Daniel B. | year = 2011 | title = Economic Professors' Favorite Economic Thinkers, Journals, and Blogs | url = http://econjwatch.org/articles/economics-professors-favorite-economic-thinkers-journals-and-blogs-along-with-party-and-policy-views | journal = Econ Journal Watch | volume = 8 | issue = 2| pages = 126–146 }}</ref> publishes his seminal text ''[[The Wealth of Nations]]''.<ref>M Skousen (2007). The Big Three in Economics: Adam Smith, Karl Marx, And John Maynard Keynes p3,5,6.</ref><ref>E. K. Hunt (2002). History of Economic Thought: A Critical Perspective, p.3. {{ISBN|0-7656-0606-2}}</ref>
* The [[Watt steam engine]], conceived in 1765, goes into production. It is the first type of steam engine to make use of steam at a pressure just above atmospheric.

;1779
* [[Samuel Crompton]] invented the [[spinning mule]], which improved the industrialised production of thread for textile manufacture. The spinning mule combined features of [[James Hargreaves]]' [[spinning jenny]] and [[Richard Arkwright]]'s [[Water Frame|water frame]].

;1781
* [[The Iron Bridge]], the first arch bridge made of [[cast iron]], is built by [[Abraham Darby III]].<ref name="oakes_atoz"/>

;1783
* A pioneer of [[selective breeding]] and [[artificial selection]], [[Robert Bakewell (agriculturalist)|Robert Bakewell]], forms the Dishley Society to promote and advance the interests of livestock breeders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert Bakewell* 1725–1795|url=http://www.ans.iastate.edu/history/faculty/bakewell/bakewell.html|publisher=Animal Science Department at Iowa State University|access-date=4 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141123061120/http://www.ans.iastate.edu/history/faculty/bakewell/bakewell.html|archive-date=23 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/history/historic_figures/bakewell_robert.shtml|title=Historic Figures* Robert Bakewell (1725–1795)|publisher=BBC|access-date=4 April 2015}}</ref>

;1786
* The [[threshing machine]] is invented by [[Andrew Meikle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.engineeringhalloffame.org/profile-meikle.html|title=Andrew Meikle (1719–1811) engineer and inventor of the threshing machine, the predecessor of the combine harvester|publisher=Scottish Engineering Hall of Fame|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref>

;1798
* [[Edward Jenner]] invents the first [[vaccine]].

==19th century==
[[File:AnalyticalMachine Babbage London.jpg|thumb|A trial model of a part of the [[Analytical Engine]], first described by [[Charles Babbage]] in 1837<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sciencemuseum.org.uk/objects/computing_and_data_processing/1878-3.aspx |title=Babbage's Analytical Engine, 1834–1871. (Trial model) |publisher=Science Museum |date=16 January 2007 |access-date=1 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100920230519/http://www.sciencemuseum.org.uk/objects/computing_and_data_processing/1878-3.aspx |archive-date=20 September 2010 }}</ref>]]

;1802
* Sir [[Humphry Davy]] creates the first [[incandescent light bulb|incandescent light]] by passing a current from a battery, at the time the world's most powerful, through a thin strip of [[platinum]].

;1804
* The world's first [[locomotive]]-hauled [[railway]] journey is made by [[Richard Trevithick]]'s [[steam locomotive]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/local/southeastwales/hi/people_and_places/history/newsid_8024000/8024766.stm|title=Trevithick the railway pioneer|date=29 April 2009|publisher=BBC|access-date=2010-12-07}}</ref>

;1807
* [[Alexander John Forsyth]] invents [[percussion ignition]], the foundation of modern [[firearms]].

;1814
* [[Robert Salmon (inventor)|Robert Salmon]] patents the first [[haymaking]] machine.

;{{Circa|1820}}
* [[John Loudon McAdam]] develops the [[Macadam]] road construction technique.

;1822
* [[Charles Babbage]] proposes the idea for a [[Difference engine]], an automatic [[mechanical calculator]] designed to tabulate [[polynomial|polynomial functions]], in a paper to the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] entitled "Note on the application of machinery to the [[computation]] of astronomical and mathematical tables".<ref>{{cite web

 |author2     = Robertson, Edmund F.
 |author-link2 = Edmund F. Robertson
 |year        = 1998

;1823
* An improved system of [[soil drainage]] is developed by [[James Smith (inventor)|James Smith]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Russell|first1=Edward J.|title=Fertility of the soil|date=2011|publisher=Cambridge Univ Press|location=Cambridge|isbn=9781107401761|page=78|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ffzwjkJY4doC&q=soil+drainage+james+smith|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref>

;1824
* [[William Aspdin]] obtains a patent for [[Portland cement]] (concrete).

;1825
* [[William Sturgeon]] invents the [[electromagnet]].

;1828
* A mechanical [[reaping machine]] is invented by [[Patrick Bell]].<ref>Journal of the Society of Arts, Volume 6 By Society of Arts (Great Britain)</ref>

;1831
* [[Electromagnetic induction]], the operating principle of [[transformer]]s and nearly all modern [[electric generators]], is discovered by [[Michael Faraday]].

;1835
* Scotsman [[James Bowman Lindsay]] invents the [[incandescent light bulb]].<ref name=Challoner>{{cite book|last=Challoner|first=Jack|title=1001 Inventions That Changed The World|publisher=Barrons Educational Series|location=Hauppauge NY|year=2009|page=305|display-authors=etal|id= {{ASIN|1844036111|country=uk}}}}</ref>

;1836
* The [[Marsh test]] for detecting [[arsenic]] poisoning is developed by [[James Marsh (chemist)|James Marsh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.history-magazine.com/arsenic.html|title=Arsenic|author=Victoria King|work=History Magazine}}</ref>

;1837
* [[Charles Babbage]] describes an [[Analytical Engine]], the first mechanical, general-purpose programmable computer.<ref name="Babbage">{{Cite web|url=https://www.fourmilab.ch/babbage/hpb1910.html|title=Babbage's Analytical Engine|website=www.fourmilab.ch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | chapter-url=http://plato.stanford.edu/entries/computing-history/ |title = The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|chapter = The Modern History of Computing|publisher = Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|year = 2017}}</ref>
* The [[Cooke and Wheatstone telegraph]], the first commercially successful [[electric telegraph]], is designed by Sir [[Charles Wheatstone]] and Sir [[William Fothergill Cooke]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cntr.salford.ac.uk/comms/johntawell.php|title=The development of the electric telegraph|publisher=University of Salford|access-date=11 May 2015}}</ref><ref name="kcl_wheatstone"/><ref name="bowers_wheatstone"/>

;1839
* A [[pedal bicycle]] is invented by [[Kirkpatrick Macmillan]].<ref name="Kirkpatrick Macmillan">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/history/historic_figures/macmillan_kirkpatrick.shtml|title=BBC – History – Kirkpatrick Macmillan|access-date=2008-12-31}}</ref>

;1840
* [[Rowland Hill (postal reformer)|Sir Rowland Hill]] reforms the postal system with [[Uniform Penny Post]] and introduces the first [[postage stamp]], the [[Penny Black]], on 1 May.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://postalheritage.wordpress.com/2009/08/21/rowland-hill%E2%80%99s-postal-reforms/|title=Private Site|website=postalheritage.wordpress.com}}</ref>

;1841
* [[Alexander Bain (inventor)|Alexander Bain]] patents his design produced the prior year for an [[electric clock]].<ref>An account of some remarkable applications of the electric fluid to the useful arts by Alexander Bain</ref>

;1842
* [[Superphosphate]], the first chemical [[fertiliser]], is patented by [[John Bennet Lawes]].{{citation needed|date=May 2018}}

;1843
* [[SS Great Britain]], the world's first steam-powered, screw propeller-driven passenger liner with an iron hull is launched. Designed by [[Isambard Kingdom Brunel]], it was at the time the largest ship afloat.
* [[Alexander Bain (inventor)|Alexander Bain]] patents a design for a [[facsimile machine]].
* [[Ada Lovelace]] recognizes the potential of the [[Analytical engine|analytics engine]] as a general purpose computer and invents [[computer programming]].

;1846
* A design for a chemical telegraph is patented by [[Alexander Bain (inventor)|Alexander Bain]]. Bain's telegraph is installed on the wires of the Electric Telegraph Company on one line. Later, in 1850, it was used in America by [[Henry O'Reilly]].<ref>Alexander Bain of Watten: genius of the North Robert P. Gunn Caithness Field Club, 1976</ref>

;1847
* [[Boolean algebra]], the basis for digital logic, is introduced by [[George Boole]] in his book ''The Mathematical Analysis of Logic''.<ref>{{Cite book
  | last = Boole
  | first = George
  | author-link = George Boole
  | title = An Investigation of the Laws of Thought
  | publisher = Prometheus Books
  | orig-year = 1854
  | year = 2003
  | isbn = 978-1-59102-089-9 }}</ref>
* [[Tom Smith (confectioner)|Tom Smith]] invents the [[Christmas cracker]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Kimpton |first=Peter |date=2005 |title=Tom Smith's Christmas Crackers: An Illustrated History |url= |location= |publisher=Tempus |page= |isbn=0-7524-3164-1 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Baker |first=Margaret |date=1992 |title=Discovering Christmas Customs and Folklore: A Guide to Seasonal Rites |url= |location= |publisher=Osprey Publishing |page=72 |isbn=0-7478-0175-4 }}</ref>

;1851
* Improvements to the [[facsimile machine]] are demonstrated by [[Frederick Bakewell]] at the [[The Great Exhibition|1851 World's Fair]] in London.

;1852
* A steam-driven ploughing engine is invented by [[John Fowler (agricultural engineer)|John Fowler]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.todayinsci.com/10/10_21.htm|title=Scientists born on October 21st|access-date=31 October 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.steamploughclub.org.uk/history.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150404171153/http://www.steamploughclub.org.uk/history.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 4, 2015|title=History of Steam Ploughing|publisher=Steam Plough Club|date=1998|access-date=4 April 2015}}</ref>

;1853
* Scottish physician [[Alexander Wood (physician)|Alexander Wood]] develops a medical hypodermic syringe with a needle fine enough to pierce the skin.<ref name=Hugh2006>{{cite book|year=2006|editor1-last=Huth|editor1-first= Edward J.|editor2-last=Murray|editor2-first=T. J.|title=Medicine in Quotations: Views of Health and Disease Through the Ages|publisher=American College of Physic|page=130}}</ref>

;1854
* The [[Playfair cipher]], the first literal digraph substitution cipher, is invented by [[Charles Wheatstone]] and later promoted for use by [[Lyon Playfair, 1st Baron Playfair|Lord Playfair]].<ref name="bowers_wheatstone">{{cite book|title=Sir Charles Wheatstone FRS: 1802–1875|author=Brian Bowers|year=2002|isbn=978-0-85296-103-2|publisher=Institution of Engineering and Technology}}</ref>

;1868
* [[Mushet steel]], the first commercial steel [[alloy]], is invented by [[Robert Forester Mushet]].
* [[Thomas Humber]] develops a bicycle design with the pedals driving the rear wheel.
* The first manually operated gas-lamp [[traffic light]]s are installed outside the [[Houses of Parliament]] on 10 December.

;1869
* A bicycle design is developed by [[Thomas McCall (inventor)|Thomas McCall]].

;1873
* Discovery of the [[photoconductivity]] of the element [[selenium]] by [[Willoughby Smith]]. This led to the invention of [[photoelectric cell]]s ([[solar panels]]), including those used in the earliest television systems.

;1876
* Scotsman [[Alexander Graham Bell]] patents the [[telephone]] in the U.S.<!--Note:Alexander Graham Bell born and raised in Scotland, made a number of inventions as a British citizen, notably the telephone in 1876; he did not become an American citizen until 1882, and spent the remaining years of his life predominately living in Canada at a summer residence.--><ref name=AHP>{{cite web|url=http://www.nls.uk/scientists/biographies/alexander-graham-bell/index.html|title=Scottish Science Hall of Fame – Alexander Graham Bell (1847–1922)|access-date=2010-02-20|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101011165704/http://digital.nls.uk/scientists/biographies/alexander-graham-bell/index.html|archive-date=2010-10-11}}</ref>
* The first [[safety bicycle]] is designed by the English engineer [[Harry John Lawson]] (also called Henry). Unlike the [[penny-farthing]], the rider's feet were within reach of the ground, making it safer to stop.

;1878
* Demonstration of an [[incandescent light bulb]] by [[Joseph Wilson Swan]].<ref>{{cite book|title=1000 Lights: 1878–1959|editor=Charlotte Fiell|editor2=Peter Fiell|isbn=978-3-8228-1606-6|publisher=Taschen GmbH|year=2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Gene cartels: biotech patents in the age of free trade|url=https://archive.org/details/genecartels00palo|url-access=limited|author=Luigi Palombi|page=[https://archive.org/details/genecartels00palo/page/n167 152]|year=2009|publisher=Edward Elgar Pub|isbn=978-1-84720-836-1}}</ref>

;1883
* The [[Fresno scraper]], which became a model for modern earth movers, is invented in California by Scottish emigrant [[James Porteous]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Fresno Scraper|url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/who-we-are/engineering-history/landmarks/158-fresno-scraper|publisher=American Society of Mechanical Engineers|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref>

;1884
* The [[light switch]] is invented by [[John Henry Holmes]], Quaker of Newcastle.
* [[Steam turbine#Reaction turbines|Reaction steam turbine]] invented by Anglo-Irish engineer [[Charles Algernon Parsons]].

;1885
* The first commercially successful safety bicycle, called the ''Rover'', is designed by [[John Kemp Starley]]. The following year [[Dan Albone]] produces a derivative of this called the ''Ivel Safety cycle''.

;1886
* [[Walter Parry Haskett Smith]], often called the ''Father of Rock Climbing'' in Britain, completes his first ascent of the [[Napes Needle]], solo and without any protective equipment.

;1892
* Sir [[Francis Galton]] devises a method for classifying [[fingerprint]]s that proved useful in [[forensic science]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.galtoninstitute.org.uk/Newsletters/GINL9909/francis_galton.htm|title=Who Is Sir Francis Galton?|publisher=Galton Institute|access-date=6 December 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110602085241/http://www.galtoninstitute.org.uk/Newsletters/GINL9909/francis_galton.htm|archive-date=2011-06-02|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;1897
* Sir [[J. J. Thomson|Joseph John Thomson]] discovers the [[electron]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Springford |first1=Michael |title=Electron: A Centenary Volume |date=1997 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9780521561303 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qUipZ0pXzfQC&pg=PA1 |language=en}}</ref>
* The world's first wireless station is established on the [[Isle of Wight]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Lee|first1=Eric|title=How internet radio can change the world : an activist's handbook|date=2005|publisher=iUniversr, Inc.|location=New York|isbn=9780595349654|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Md0aYx9jql8C&q=The+world%27s+first+radio+station+on+the+Isle+of+Wight&pg=PA7|access-date=22 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The origins of radio |url=http://www.connected-earth.com/Journeys/Firstgenerationtechnologies/Awirelessworld/Theoriginsofradio/index.htm |publisher=Connected Earth |access-date=22 March 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402110146/http://www.connected-earth.com/Journeys/Firstgenerationtechnologies/Awirelessworld/Theoriginsofradio/index.htm |archive-date= 2 April 2015 }}</ref>

==20th century==
[[File:Colossus.jpg|thumb|A [[Colossus computer]], developed by British codebreakers in 1943–1945]]

;1901
* The first wireless signal across the Atlantic is sent from Cornwall in England and received in Newfoundland in Canada (a distance of 2,100 miles) by Italian scientist [[Guglielmo Marconi]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Marconi sends first Atlantic wireless transmission|date=9 February 2010 |url=http://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/marconi-sends-first-atlantic-wireless-transmission|publisher=History|access-date=13 December 2016}}</ref>
* The first commercially successful light farm [[tractor]] is patented by [[Dan Albone]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biggleswadehistory.org.uk/Dan%20Albone.htm |title=Dan Albone |publisher=Biggleswade History Society |access-date=30 August 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315090452/http://www.biggleswadehistory.org.uk/Dan%20Albone.htm |archive-date=15 March 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scienceandsociety.co.uk/results.asp?image=10307483&wwwflag=2&imagepos=1|title=Dan Albone, English inventor, 1902|publisher=The Science and Society Picture Library}}</ref>

;1902
* [[Edgar Purnell Hooley]] develops [[Tarmacadam|Tarmac]].

;1906
* The introduction of {{HMS|Dreadnought|1906|6}}, a revolutionary capital ship design.

;1907
* [[Henry Joseph Round]] discovers [[electroluminescence]], the principle behind [[LED]]s.

;1910
* The first formal driving school, the [[British School of Motoring]], is founded in London.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/motoring/road-safety/7937429/100-years-of-the-driving-lesson.html | location=London | work=The Daily Telegraph | title=100 Years Of The Driving Lesson | first=David | last=Williams | date=2010-08-19}}</ref>
* [[Frank Barnwell]] establishes the fundamentals of [[aerospace engineering|aircraft design]] at the University of Glasgow,<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.worldchanging.glasgow.ac.uk/article/?id=4 |title = University of Glasgow :: World Changing:: Establishing fundamental principles in aircraft design}}</ref> having made the first powered flight in Scotland the previous year.

;1916
* The first use in battle of the military [[tank]] (although the tank was also developed independently elsewhere).

;1918
* The [[Royal Air Force]] becomes the first independent air force in the world.<ref>Royal Air Force 90th Anniversary History of the RAF</ref>
* The introduction of [[HMS Argus (I49)|HMS Argus]] the first example of the standard pattern of aircraft carrier, with a full-length flight deck that allowed wheeled aircraft to take off and land.

;1922
* In [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]], France, Englishman Edwin Belin demonstrates a mechanical scanning device, an early precursor to modern [[television]].

;1926
* [[John Logie Baird]] makes the first public demonstration of a [[mechanical television]] on 26 January (the first successful transmissions were in early 1923 and February 1924). Later, in July 1928, he demonstrated the first [[colour television]].<ref name="John Logie Baird">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/history/historic_figures/baird_logie.shtml|title=BBC – History – John Logie Baird|access-date=2008-12-31}}</ref><ref name=ADP>[http://www.bairdtelevision.com/colour.html The World's First High Definition Colour Television System]. McLean, p. 196.</ref>

;1930
* The [[jet engine]] is patented by Sir [[Frank Whittle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/history/historic_figures/whittle_frank.shtml|title=Frank Whittle (1907–1996)|publisher=BBC|access-date=2010-12-06}}</ref>

;1932
* The [[Anglepoise lamp]] is patented by George Carwardine, a design consultant specialising in vehicle suspension systems.

;1933
* The [[Cat's eye (road)|Cat's eye]] road marking is invented by [[Percy Shaw]] and patented the following year.

;1936
* English economist [[John Maynard Keynes]] publishes his work ''[[The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money]]'' which challenged the established [[classical economics]] and led to the [[Keynesian Revolution]] in the way economists thought.
* The world's first public broadcasts of [[405-line television system|high-definition television]] are made from [[Alexandra Palace]], North London, by the [[BBC Television Service]]. It is the first fully electronic television system to be used in regular [[broadcasting]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Burns|first1=Russell|title=Communications: an international history of the formative years|date=2004|publisher=Inst. of Electrical Engineers|isbn=9780863413278|page=541|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7eUUy8-VvwoC&pg=PA541}}</ref>

;1937
* First available in the London area, the [[999 (emergency telephone number)|999]] telephone number is introduced as the world's first [[Emergency telephone number|emergency telephone service]].

;1939
* The initial design of the [[Bombe]], an electromechanical device to assist with the deciphering of messages encrypted by the [[Enigma machine]], is produced by [[Alan Turing]] at the [[Government Code and Cypher School]] at [[Bletchley Park]].<ref name="Turing" />

;1943
* [[Colossus computer]] begins working, the world's first electronic digital programmable computer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ivorcatt.com/47c.htm|title=Colossus; Thomas H Flowers; Bletchley Park; Howard Champaigne; Allen W. M. Coombs; W. W. Chandler|website=www.ivorcatt.com|access-date=2011-09-11|archive-date=2006-03-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060326041703/http://www.ivorcatt.com/47c.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;1949
* The [[Manchester Mark 1]] computer, significant because of its pioneering inclusion of [[index registers]], ran its first programme error free. Its chief designers are [[Frederic Calland Williams|Freddie Williams]] and [[Tom Kilburn]].

;1951
* The concept of [[microprogramming]] is developed by [[Maurice Wilkes]] from the realisation that the CPU of a computer could be controlled by a miniature, highly specialised computer program in high-speed [[Read-only memory|ROM]].
* [[LEO (computer)|LEO]] is the first business application (a payroll system) on an electronic computer.

;1952
* The introduction of the [[de Havilland Comet]] the world's first commercial [[jet airliner]].
* [[Autocode]], regarded as the first compiled programming language, is developed for the Manchester Mark 1 by [[Alick Glennie]].

;1953
* Englishman [[Francis Crick]] and American [[James Watson]] of [[Cavendish Laboratory]] in the [[University of Cambridge]], analysed X-ray crystallography data taken by [[Rosalind Franklin]] of [[King's College London]], to decipher the double helical structure of DNA. They share the 1962 [[Nobel Prize in Medicine]] for their work.<ref>{{cite web | year =2014| url =https://www.bbc.co.uk/history/historic_figures/crick_and_watson.shtml| title = Crick and Watson (1916–2004)| work=BBC History| publisher =BBC | access-date =21 February 2016 }}</ref>

;1955
* The first accurate atomic clock, a caesium standard based on a certain transition of the caesium-133 atom, is built by [[Louis Essen]] at the National Physical Laboratory.  This clock enabled further development of general relativity, and started a basis for an enhanced SI unit system.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=L. Essen, J.V.L. Parry|year=1955|title=An Atomic Standard of Frequency and Time Interval – A Caesium Resonator|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=176|issue=4476 |pages=280–282|doi=10.1038/176280a0|bibcode=1955Natur.176..280E|s2cid=4191481}}</ref>

;1956
* [[Metrovick 950]], the first commercial [[transistor computer]], is built by the [[Metropolitan-Vickers]] company.

;1961
* The first electronic desktop [[calculator]]s, the [[Sumlock ANITA calculator|ANITA Mk7 and ANITA Mk8]], are manufactured by the [[Bell Punch|Bell Punch Company]] and marketed by its [[Sumlock Comptometer]] division.

;1963
* High strength [[carbon fibre]] is invented by engineers at the [[Royal Aircraft Establishment]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The history and uses of carbon fibre|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p013jv1v|publisher=BBC|access-date=3 May 2015|date=9 January 2013}}</ref>
* The [[Lava lamp]] is invented by British accountant [[Edward Craven Walker]].

;1964
* The first theory of the [[Higgs boson]] is put forward by [[Peter Higgs]], a particle-physics theorist at the [[University of Edinburgh]], and five other physicists.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-22073080|title=Peter Higgs: Behind the scenes at the Universe|work=BBC News |date=April 8, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ph.ed.ac.uk/higgs|title=Peter Higgs and the Higgs Boson|date=March 12, 2017|website=School of Physics and Astronomy}}</ref> The particle is discovered in 2012 at [[CERN]]'s [[Large Hadron Collider]] and its existence is confirmed in 2013.

;1965
* A pioneer of the development of [[dairy farming]] systems, [[Rex Paterson]], set out his principles for labour management.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.nuffield.ox.ac.uk/economics/history/paper27/27grant.pdf|last1=Grant|first1=Oliver|title=The Diffusion Of The Herringbone Parlour* A Case Study In The History Of Agricultural Technology|journal=University of Oxford Discussion Papers in Economic and Social History|date=December 1998|issue=27|page=8|access-date=4 April 2015}}</ref>
* The Touchscreen was invented by E. A. Johnson working at the Radar Research Establishment, Malvern, Worcestershire.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://mraths.org.uk/?page_id=531 | title=1965 – the Touchscreen| date=2016-02-05}}</ref>
* The [[Automated external defibrillator|portable defibrillator]] was invented and tested in Belfast by [[Frank Pantridge]]<ref>{{Citation |title=Frank Pantridge |date=2026-02-18 |work=Wikipedia |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Frank_Pantridge&oldid=1339002257 |access-date=2026-04-02 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Father of Emergency Medicine |url=https://www.ulstertransportmuseum.org/stories/father-emergency-medicine |access-date=2026-04-02 |website=www.ulstertransportmuseum.org |language=en}}</ref>

;1966
* The [[cash machine]] and [[personal identification number]] system are patented by [[James Goodfellow]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Batiz-Lazo|first1=Bernardo|last2=Reid|first2=Robert J. K.|title=Evidence from the Patent Record on the Development of Cash Dispensing Technology|url=http://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/9461/1/MPRA_paper_9461.pdf|publisher=Munich Personal RePEc Archive|access-date=27 April 2015|date=30 June 2008|page=3}}</ref>

;1969
* The first [[Carbon (fibre)|carbon fibre]] fabric in the world is weaved in [[Stockport]], England.<ref>{{cite web|title=About Us|url=http://www.carrreinforcements.com/about.htm|publisher=Carr Reinforcements|access-date=3 May 2015|archive-date=9 October 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081009220714/http://www.carrreinforcements.com/about.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

;1970
* One of the first [[handheld television]]s, the [[MTV-1]], is developed by Sir [[Clive Sinclair]].

;1973
* [[Clifford Cocks]] develops the algorithm for the [[RSA cipher]] while working at the [[Government Communications Headquarters]], approximately three years before it was independently developed by Rivest, Shamir and Adleman at [[MIT]]. The British government declassified the 1973 invention in 1997.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Code Book |author=Simon Singh|author-link=Simon Singh|year=2000|isbn=978-0-385-49531-8|publisher=Fourth Estate|title-link=The Code Book}}</ref>

;1976
* [[M. Stanley Whittingham]] develops the first [[Lithium-ion battery]], while working as a researcher for [[ExxonMobil]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Whittingham|first=M. S.|date=1976-06-01|title=Electrical Energy Storage and Intercalation Chemistry|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1976Sci...192.1126W|journal=Science|volume=192|issue=4244|pages=1126–1127|doi=10.1126/science.192.4244.1126|pmid=17748676|bibcode=1976Sci...192.1126W|s2cid=36607505|issn=0036-8075}}</ref>

;1977
* Steptoe and Edwards successfully carried out a pioneering conception which resulted in the birth of the world's first baby to be conceived by [[IVF]], [[Louise Brown]] on 25 July 1978, in [[Oldham General Hospital]], Greater Manchester, UK.<ref>{{Cite news | title = 1978: First 'test tube baby' born | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/july/25/newsid_2499000/2499411.stm | work = BBC | access-date =13 June 2009 | quote = The birth of the world's first "test tube baby" has been announced in Manchester (England). Louise Brown was born shortly before midnight in Oldham and District General Hospital | date=25 July 1978}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | title = World's first test-tube baby Louise Brown has a child of her own | url = https://www.independent.co.uk/life-style/health-and-families/health-news/worlds-first-testtube-baby-louise-brown-has-a-child-of-her-own-432080.html |work=The Independent | access-date =5 May 2010
| quote = The 28-year-old, whose pioneering conception by in-vitro fertilisation made her famous around the world.. The fertility specialists [[Patrick Steptoe]] and [[Robert Geoffrey Edwards|Bob Edwards]] became the first to successfully carry out IVF by extracting an egg, impregnating it with sperm and planting the resulting embryo back into the mother | location=London | first=Cole | last=Moreton | date=14 January 2007}}</ref><ref>Schulman, Joseph D. (2010) ''Robert G. Edwards – A Personal Viewpoint'', CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform, {{ISBN|1456320750}}.</ref>

;1979
* The [[tree shelter]] is invented by Graham Tuley to protect tree seedlings.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Using Tree Shelters To Establish Northern Red Oak And Other Hardwoods|url=http://archive.lib.msu.edu/DMC/Ag.%20Ext.%202007-Chelsie/PDF/e2584.pdf|journal=Michigan State University Extension Bulletin|access-date=5 April 2015|date=May 1997|page=2|last1=Lantagne|first1=D. O. }}</ref>
* One of the first [[laptop computer]]s, the [[GRiD Compass]], is designed by [[Bill Moggridge]].

;1984
* [[DNA profiling]] is discovered by Sir [[Alec Jeffreys]] at the [[University of Leicester]].
* One of the world's first [[computer game]]s to use [[3D graphics]], [[Elite (video game)|Elite]], is developed by [[David Braben]] and [[Ian Bell]].

;1989
* Sir [[Tim Berners-Lee]] writes a proposal for what will become the [[World Wide Web]]. The following year, he specified HTML, the hypertext language, and HTTP, the protocol.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.w3.org/People/Berners-Lee/FAQ.html|title=Frequently asked questions|publisher=Tim Berners-Lee|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref>
* The [[Touchpad]] pointing device is first developed for [[Psion (computers)|Psion computers]].

;1991
* A patent for an [[iris recognition]] algorithm is filed by [[John Daugman]] while working at the [[University of Cambridge]] which became the basis of all publicly deployed iris recognition systems.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.freepatentsonline.com/5291560.html|title=Biometric personal identification system based on iris analysis|date=March 1994 |access-date=2010-12-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Research Excellence Framework|url=http://impact.ref.ac.uk/CaseStudies/CaseStudy.aspx?Id=16707|website=Research Excellence Framework|publisher=Iris Recognition|access-date=25 April 2015}}</ref>
* The source code for the world's first [[web browser]], called [[WorldWideWeb]] (later renamed Nexus to avoid confusion with the [[World Wide Web]]), is released into the public domain by Sir [[Tim Berners-Lee]].

;1992
* The first [[SMS]] message in the world is sent over the UK's GSM network.

;1995
* The world's first national [[DNA database]] is developed.<ref>{{cite news|title=DNA: timeline of the national DNA database|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/politics/5289062/DNA-timeline-of-the-national-DNA-database.html|newspaper=The Telegraph|access-date=25 April 2015|date=7 May 2009}}</ref>

;1996
*  [[Animal cloning]], a female domestic sheep became the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell, by scientists at the [[Roslin Institute]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = McLaren | first1 = A | year = 2000 | title = Cloning: pathways to a pluripotent future | journal = Science | volume = 288 | issue = 5472| pages = 1775–80 | doi = 10.1126/science.288.5472.1775 | pmid = 10877698 | s2cid = 44320353 }}</ref>

;1997
* Scottish scientists at the Roslin Institute in Edinburgh, produce the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.<ref>{{cite web | year =2008| url =https://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/february/22/newsid_4245000/4245877.stm | title = Dolly the Sheep is Cloned| work=On This Day... | publisher =BBC | access-date =21 February 2016 }}</ref>
* The [[ThrustSSC]] jet-propelled car, designed and built in England, sets the [[land speed record]].

==21st century==

;2003
* [[Beagle 2]], a British landing spacecraft that forms part of the [[European Space Agency]]'s 2003 [[Mars Express]] mission lands on the surface of Mars but fails to communicate. It is located twelve years later in a series of images from [[NASA]]'s [[Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter]] that suggest two of Beagle's four solar panels failed to deploy, blocking the spacecraft's communications antenna.

;2004
* [[Graphene]] is isolated from graphite at the [[University of Manchester]] by [[Andre Geim]] and [[Konstantin Novoselov]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Story of Graphene|url=http://www.graphene.manchester.ac.uk/explore/the-story-of-graphene/|publisher=University of Manchester|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref>

;2005
* The design for a machine to lay rail track, the "Trac Rail Transposer", is patented and goes on to be used by [[Network Rail]] in the United Kingdom and the [[New York City Subway]] in the United States.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ayrshire brothers' invention to transform America's railways|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/uk-scotland-36459486|access-date=7 June 2016|work=BBC|date=6 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Laying lines|journal=Railway Strategies|date=6 January 2014|issue=103|url=http://www.railwaystrategies.co.uk/article-page.php?contentid=19184&issueid=539|access-date=7 June 2016|archive-date=26 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220426070900/http://www.railwaystrategies.co.uk/article-page.php?contentid=19184&issueid=539|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=US Patent Application No: 2008/0072,783 – Railway Rail Handling Apparatus and Method|url=http://www.patentbuddy.com/Patent/20080072783|website=PatentBuddy|access-date=7 June 2016}}</ref>

;2010
* Ambulight PDT, a light-emitting plaster, or "sticker," designed for photodynamic therapy to treat non-melanoma skin cancers

;2012
* [[Raspberry Pi]],  a single-board computer, is launched and quickly becomes popular for education in programming and computer science.<ref>{{cite news|title=Raspberry Pi becomes best selling British computer|url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2015/feb/18/raspberry-pi-becomes-best-selling-british-computer|access-date=22 March 2015|newspaper=The Guardian|date=18 February 2015}}</ref>

;2014
* The [[European Space Agency]]'s [[Philae (spacecraft)|Philae]] lander leaves the [[Rosetta (spacecraft)|Rosetta]] spacecraft and makes the first ever landing on a comet. The Philae lander was built with significant British expertise and technology, alongside that of several other countries.<ref>{{cite news|title=UK space industry behind Rosetta comet mission|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/industry/engineering/11221945/UK-space-industry-behind-Rosetta-comet-mission.html|newspaper=The Telegraph|access-date=4 May 2015|date=11 November 2014|last1=Tovey|first1=Alan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Europe makes history with first ever comet landing|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/europe-makes-history-with-first-ever-comet-landing|publisher=UK Space Agency|access-date=4 May 2015|date=12 November 2014}}</ref>

The following is a list and timeline of innovations as well as inventions and discoveries that involved British people or the United Kingdom including the predecessor states before the Treaty of Union in 1707, the Kingdom of England and the Kingdom of Scotland. This list covers, but is not limited to, innovation and invention in the mechanical, electronic, and industrial fields, as well as medicine, military devices and theory, artistic and scientific discovery and innovation, and ideas in religion and ethics.
Factors that historians note spurred innovation and discovery include the 17th century Scientific Revolution and the 18th/19th century Industrial Revolution. Another possible influence is the British patent system which had medieval origins and was codified with the Patent Law Amendment Act 1852 (15 & 16 Vict. c. 83).
